[AMD][ConSan] Support async-copy mbarrier arrive (#12320)

Instrument `amdg.async_copy_mbarrier_arrive` using the existing
async-copy barrier tracking. A wait on the corresponding barrier phase
completes the arrive and publishes the covered async loads. The
`async_copy_mbarrier_arrive` does not track async stores.

Use a separate `AsyncCopyMbarrierArrive` peer class for these arrivals.
Sharing the TDM peer class would let a wait on a TDM barrier complete
async-copy arrivals pending on other barriers. The class is allocated
only when a target hook opts in; NVIDIA's cp.async arrive stays on the
TMA class.

Add lit and gfx1250 runtime coverage and check that NVIDIA arrivals
retain their existing peer class.

[triton-ext] Version libtriton's exported symbols as TRITON

With TRITON_EXT_ENABLED=ON, libtriton exports all its symbols, including
its statically linked LLVM and MLIR, so extensions can link against
them. These exports are unversioned. If another LLVM is loaded into the
process with RTLD_GLOBAL, the two copies bind to each other's symbols.
ROCm torch preloads ROCm's libLLVM.so, which leads to these failures:

- `import torch; import triton` segfaults because libtriton binds to
  ROCm's LLVM.
- Loading an extension before torch aborts with "LLVM ERROR: Option
  'default' already exists!" because ROCm's LLVM binds to libtriton.

On Linux, TRITON_EXT_ENABLED builds now link libtriton with the version
script `TRITON { global: *; };`. The set of exported symbols stays the
same, but each one is now sym@@TRITON. References from libtriton and its
extensions therefore no longer match another library's sym@LLVM_<N>,
and the reverse holds too. Upstream libLLVM.so uses the same mechanism.

Builds without TRITON_EXT_ENABLED and macOS/Windows builds are
unchanged. Existing extensions still load, but they need a rebuild to
pick up the versioned references.

Clean up the Gluon block-scaled matmul example (#12627)

This cleanup paves the way for planned Rubin optimizations while keeping
the example focused and readable. Remove autotuning and the cuBLAS
comparison, make launch options explicit, and construct TMA descriptors
directly. Preserve the best configs and scheduler heuristic. Test best
configs with both schedulers over small and odd shapes, including Rubin
double buffering. Benchmark 1CTA versus 2CTA on a small K sweep with MN
shapes suited to each architecture.

[NVIDIA][Gluon] Support FP6 shared tiles for TMA and tcgen05 (#12548)

First in a stack of three PRs. #12541 builds on this to add the
conversion and compacting TMA store for regular Triton kernels.

Gluon's `NVMMASharedLayout` describes physical packing. Use
`padding="b6x16_p32"` for a TMA load or MMA operand. Each 16-byte atom
contains 12 packed bytes followed by four padding bytes. Use
`padding="b6p2x16"` for a TMA store. Each byte holds a code in its low
six bits. TMA compacts 128 of these lanes into 96 bytes in global
memory. [PTX FP6
packing](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#tensor-dimension-size-format-sub-bytes-padding-align-b6-p2-16).

Specify the numerical formats on the MMA operation, for example
`tcgen05_mma(a, b, acc, a_type="e2m3", b_type="e3m2")`. Plain and scaled
MMA can use different formats for two operands with the same packing. A
generic per-element linear-layout query fails for the packed load
format. TMA, MMA and allocation analysis use physical offsets at
whole-atom boundaries.

This PR uses 128-value boxes with host- or device-built tensor maps.
Coordinates count logical FP6 values and outer strides count bytes.
Draft #12614 adds the SM103-specific 64-value host store.

Built independently on GB300. All 18 focused GPU cases and four MLIR
test files passed, including mixed E2M3/E3M2 MMA, transposed operands,
and existing FP4 coverage.

[NVIDIA] Update ptxas to 13.5.37 (#12626)

Update ptxas from 13.4.59 to 13.5.37, released with CUDA 13.5.

Verified Triton's Linux x86-64 and SBSA download URLs against NVIDIA's
release manifest, downloaded both archives, and checked their SHA-256
hashes and embedded PTXAS versions. GPU validation will run in CI.

[BC Breaking][NVIDIA] Lower more operations through LLVM and NVVM (#12212)

Replace inline PTX with LLVM/NVVM operations and intrinsics where they
preserve semantics and generate equivalent or better SASS:

- **Square roots:** `math.sqrt` → `llvm.sqrt` with `afn`; `math.rsqrt` →
NVVM `rsqrt`.
- **Packed arithmetic:** FP16/BF16/FP32 add, subtract, and multiply,
plus FP16/BF16 FMA → LLVM vector operations; FP16/BF16 min/max →
`llvm.minimumnum` / `llvm.maximumnum`. Keep packed FP32 FMA in PTX to
avoid register spills from instruction sinking.
- **FP8 conversions** use NVVM conversion ops and LLVM arithmetic. SM89
needs PTX 8.1 for native FP8 conversions. On targets with SM100f,
SM110f, or SM120f features, packed BF16-to-FP8 starts at PTX 9.1 and
FP8-to-BF16 at PTX 9.2. The FP8-to-BF16 fallback through native FP16
uses the rounded conversion from #12237.
- **Integer and BF16 casts:** selected `i1` → FP16/BF16, signed `i8` →
BF16, and BF16 → FP32 paths → LLVM selects, casts, and bit operations.
- **Global memory:** unpredicated default-cache tensor loads/stores →
LLVM `load` / `store`. Keep scalar loads in PTX to avoid a ptxas
FP8-reduction miscompile.
- **Atomics** use LLVM for eligible unpredicated scalar RMWs and shared
wrapping increments. Fold all-true source masks while preserving thread
election. Use native PTX for supported 16-bit floating adds to preserve
access width, and diagnose unsupported subword shared scatter
operations.
- **Compare-and-swap:** unpredicated 32-/64-bit CAS and instrumentation
lock acquisition → LLVM `cmpxchg`.
- **Async memory** uses NVVM for eligible global-to-shared copies and
naturally aligned, unpredicated 32- and 64-bit shared stores. PTX 9.2
also supports 128-bit shared stores. Dynamic copy masks retain the PTX
ignore-source predicate.

Preserve predication, rounding, memory ordering, and synchronization
scopes. Retain PTX fallbacks for unsupported or regressing forms.

Remove the legacy SM75 MMA lowering in a separate preceding commit.
Triton [documents NVIDIA support starting at compute capability
8.0](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/8627ec5be64b6d5767edf313668de2e145a2718b/README.md#compatibility),
and [Gluon’s `mma_v2` requires the Ampere `[2, 0]`
layout](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/8627ec5be64b6d5767edf313668de2e145a2718b/python/triton/experimental/gluon/language/nvidia/ampere/__init__.py#L117).
The old SM75 `[2, 1]` path was still reachable when explicitly targeted;
this removes that unsupported functionality.
